messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 22 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Peak mix consolidation + slot sizing — follow-up & action items

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap and concrete asks so we can size capacity accurately. Great to hear about the two traffic paths (conversational help + checkout validation). Notes below and proposed next steps.

High-level throughput targets you gave (from Alex):
- Steady-state QPS: ~80 requests/sec (mostly short conversational turns)
- Peak windows: spikes up to ~520 QPS for short bursts (1–5 minutes) tied to marketing events
- Avg tokens per response: ~900 tokens (conversational), ~250 tokens (checkout validation)
- Streaming: yes for conversational flows (client streams tokens-as-they-generate)
- Target tail latency: p95 ideally <300ms for checkout paths, p95 <500ms acceptable for general chat

What we need from you to finalize sizing:
1) 24–72 hours of anonymized request logs or a sampled payload set (headers, request size, response token counts).
2) Confirmation of expected peak window durations (are spikes typically <60s, ~3m, or up to 10m?).
3) A small set of sample prompts (900-token average) and the checkout payloads (250 tokens) so we can run tokenization and end-to-end latency estimates.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Alex (NimbleCart): share sample payloads + a short description of event-driven triggers (ETA: Tue 6/26).
- Marissa: prepare a dedicated config recommendation for steady vs peak routing and whether Dedicated capacity or Hosted with fallback makes sense (ETA: Mon 6/25).
- Karthik: run a quick tokenization pass on provided samples and estimate tokens/sec for our runtime (ETA: after samples).
- Tessa: draft an initial slot/slot-mix recommendation and cost delta for 1-month pilot (ETA: Wed 6/27).

Attachments: Quick sizing matrix & template to populate — [Attachment: nimble_sizing_matrix.csv (CSV, 18KB)].

Short ask in 1 line: Alex — can you confirm peak duration (typical) and drop the sample payloads into the Drive link? That will let us produce an initial slot mix and latency projection.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Tessa — appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:
- Peak durations: typically 90–180 seconds for marketing-driven bursts, occasionally up to ~6 minutes during heavy promotions. Rarely longer than 10m.
- Steady-state is closer to 70–85 QPS.
- Token counts are estimates — conversational is ~700–1,100 tokens depending on context; checkout validation ~200–300.
- Streaming: yes, chat agents stream tokens; we expect many long-lived streams but at modest concurrency (20–30 concurrent streaming sessions during steady-state, up to ~200 during peaks).

I've uploaded two files to the shared Drive: request_samples_redacted.json (contains sampled requests) and event_timeline.csv.
Drive: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1nImbL_sizing_matrix

Propose a short follow-up technical review Wed 6/27 at 11am PT to align on slot mix and pilot length. Alex — does that work?

Subject: Re: Peak mix consolidation + slot sizing — follow-up & action items

Alex / team — I pulled the samples and ran a quick tokenization pass overnight. Preliminary numbers (very rough):
- Conversational avg tokens (sample): ~860 tokens per response (std dev ~140)
- Checkout validation avg: ~260 tokens
- Effective token savings with prefix caching on sample: ~38% (depends on how many prompt fragments are identical)

Sizing implication (initial pilot recommendation):
- Baseline steady capacity: size slots to handle 90 QPS at 860 tokens/res with caching applied (~55% of raw token cost).
- Peak buffer: ability to absorb ~520 QPS for 3m windows. Two practical approaches:
  1) Dedicated slots: 3 steady slots + 3 burst slots (auto-attach during windows),
  2) Hosted fallback: 3 steady Dedicated + Hosted overflow with routing policy (faster to deploy, slightly higher unit cost).

We still need: CPU/bandwidth profile for streaming clients (samples gave ~1.1KB/sec per open stream on average) and whether NimbleCart requires p99 latency SLAs for checkout flows. If p99 is required, we should adjust slot counts upward by ~25%.

Next steps I’ll take: finalize a slot-mix doc and a quick cost/latency tradeoff table (ETA: Tue 6/27 morning).
